configs.description: The only published configuration. Two fixed load-sharing -48 VDC supplies, no fans at all, filter slot blanked. The datasheet's ordering section lists the base model and no variants, so there is one row and it carries no part number.
configs.name: dc

gaps.wanted: A figure or drawing of this faceplate that can carry a dimension. THE ONE THAT EXISTS CANNOT, AND THE PROOF IS A STANDARD IT CONTRADICTS. Its SFP cage pitch reads 14.7-14.75 measured two ways - across the four cage bores and across the shell walls between them - against the SFF-8432 figure of 14.25 that the registry carries and that the CSR200's figure reproduces at 14.22. Its RJ-45 cell pitch reads 14.4 against a registry 13.97, the same three percent high. And its DC terminal blocks read about eleven percent SMALL against the sibling's. Nothing reconciles those with one scale. THE OBVIOUS EXPLANATION WAS TESTED AND FAILED. A perspective render would taper: panel height sampled along x is flat on both faces, 425-419 px across the CSR200 and 425-430 across this one, and the CSR180's absolute feature POSITIONS line up with the CSR200's to a millimetre or two over the whole 440. What is wrong is local scale, not geometry - the art is honeycomb dark-on-dark at low contrast and repeated careful reads of one feature wobble by 0.5 to 1 mm where the CSR200's repeat to 0.05. WHAT WAS DONE ABOUT IT: every standard part takes its size from the registry - SFP 14.25, RJ-45 13.97, USB-A, SMB - and the figure supplies POSITIONS and COUNTS only. That is the division docs/modelling-a-device.md already draws for ganged pitch, applied to the whole face. The two non-standard parts, common/dc-terminal-24@1 and edgecore/filter-slot-5915-16x@1, are sized from edge POSITIONS for the same reason, and each says so.

Which of the four stacked RJ-45 positions is which. The face carries two 1x2 stacks - four jacks - and the datasheet names only THREE non-traffic RJ-45s: the console (callout 4), the ToD/1PPS (callout 10) and the management port (callout 11). There is no BITS port on this model, which is the CSR200's callout 4 and the reason that device has twelve callouts and this one eleven. The silkscreen under the left stack is a single lamp and legend where the CSR200 has two, and it is not legible at 9.63 px/mm. So the fourth position is either blank or something unlisted, and the three that are named are placed here in the CSR200's order - console top right, management bottom right, ToD/1PPS bottom left - which is an INFERENCE FROM THE SIBLING, not a reading.

A figure of any face but the front. Neither document draws one. The quick start's step 3 does picture the grounding point - a two-hole lug on the SIDE panel near the rear, with the earth symbol beside it - which is more than the CSR200's quick start gives, but a three-quarter view of a corner fixes no coordinate, so the lug is not placed. The side panels matter more here than on any other device in this family: this box is cooled by air someone else moves across it.

An LED table. Neither document has one, and unlike the CSR200's quick start this one does not even state that the PSU lamps come up green. Five system lamps are legible - LOC, DIAG, PSU1, PSU2, ALARM - and every lamp here carries `off` and one green `on`, borrowed from edgecore/csr200 where a quick-start sentence supports it. Borrowed, and said to be.
Which of each optical port's two bezel lamps is link and which is activity - the same silence as on the CSR200, from the same vendor, about the same bezel.

Whether an air filter is sold for this model at all. The CSR200's datasheet lists two filter accessories with part numbers; this one's ordering section lists the base model and nothing else, yet the faceplate carries a filter slot and callout 5 calls it "Filter Slot (Optional)". So the bay is real, the cover is drawn, and what goes in it is unnamed by the vendor.

one of `power-max-w`, `power-max-ac-w`, `power-max-dc-w` in `attrs.power`; one of `operating-temp`, `operating-temp-f2b`, `operating-temp-b2f` in `attrs.environmental` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 1 bay (front 1); `physical-context` on port groups rj45, sfp, sfp-plus - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays
the Nautobot exporter is not importable - unlocks NetBox / Nautobot device-type export

chassis.note: datasheet - "Dimensions (WxDxH): 440 x 240 x 44 mm (17.32 x 9.45 x 1.73 in)" and "Weight: 3.8 kg (8.38 lb), with two installed PSUs", both identical to the CSR200's. The quick start does not restate them. 440 is the body width: "Installations to standard 19", 21" and 23" rack" makes the brackets an accessory outside it.

cooling.note: THIS BOX HAS NO FANS AND THAT IS WHY THE FACEPLATE LOOKS LIKE THIS. The datasheet calls the AS5915-16X a fanless, passively cooled platform and asks that it be deployed in external airflow, front-to-back or back-to-front, of at least 1 m/s measured at any point on the product surface. So `airflow: passive` rather than a direction - the datasheet names both directions as acceptable and neither as the product's - and the front plate is honeycombed edge to edge where the CSR200's is solid with perforated columns. It is also why there is no FAN lamp: five system lamps are printed, LOC DIAG PSU1 PSU2 ALARM, with the CSR200's FAN position simply empty.

figure-choice.note: Gate 1. Page 2 rendered at 600 dpi; panel found by row/column darkness at (364,1199)-(4600,1628), 4237 x 430 px, aspect 9.8535 against 10.0 for 440/44 - 1.47 percent out, which is BETTER than the CSR200's 1.86 and is not the point. See the `figure-fidelity` gap: the aspect passes and the art still will not carry a dimension, which is a case docs/modelling-a-device.md's four-percent rule does not cover. Positions it does carry, and positions are what is taken. THE QUICK START HAS NO ELEVATION. Its only hardware drawing is step 3's grounding illustration, a three-quarter view of the rear corner. That is the source for the lug being on the side panel and for nothing else.

optical-lamps.note: Four lamps per optical column, as on the CSR200: `(down) (up) (down) (up)` in the bezel between the rows, two for the upper port and two for the lower. The SFP+ offsets inside a shell - 1.78/5.14/9.00/12.41 - are measured here, on both shells, agreeing to 0.11 mm. THE SFP BLOCK'S ARE BORROWED from edgecore/csr200, whose figure resolves them on four columns to 0.06 mm where this one does not resolve them at all; the bezel is the same part and the two devices' SFP+ offsets agree to 0.25, which is what makes the borrow checkable rather than convenient.

panel-layout.note: EVERY NUMBER BELOW IS A POSITION, AND EVERY STANDARD SIZE IS A REGISTRY LOOKUP. That division is forced by the figure - see `figure-fidelity` in gaps - and it is the division docs/modelling-a-device.md already draws for ganged pitch, applied to the rest of the face for the same reason. Read at 9.6295 px/mm from crops at 19-44 px/mm with a millimetre rule burned in, because thresholds do not work on honeycomb: the two SFP+ shells centre on 180.85 and 209.50, the SFP block on 261.30, the RJ-45 block on 312.10, the two management stacks on 356.80 and 378.35, the four coax jacks on 239.11/253.96/268.71/283.51, the five system lamps on 191.30/198.50/206.00/213.10/227.20, and the USB on 152.50.

sources.note: Two documents, both staged and both docling-converted, MEASURED OFF THE PDF PAGE RATHER THAN THE CONVERTED FIGURES. csr180-datasheet (the CSR180 / AS5915-16X data sheet) carries the specification list, the ordering line, the eleven-callout front elevation on page 2, and the passive-cooling paragraph. csr180-qsg is the AS5915-16X quick start guide; it has NO front elevation at all - its only hardware art is the grounding step, which is where the side-panel lug comes from.
